summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — LITE +9%, FIX +7%, P +7%, COHR +7%, BE +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (FICO -13%, CHTR -6%, SKYD -5%, DASH -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: FICO (-13.10%) — No confirmed driver for 2026-10-27 found. Searches only returned older FICO selloffs (FHFA/Pulte criticism, VantageScore mortgage competition, price-target cuts), so this is likely a continuation of that regulatory/competition overhang. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: FICO is a mid/large-cap financial-data/software name that no strategy's universe includes, so no filter evaluated it. A single-day -13% gap on an unscheduled headline would also fail gap-size and RSI filters, and the bot likely has no short capability.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found. Likely continuation of the AI optical rally: StoneX initiated Buy with a $1,200 target and the CEO said AI components are 'sold out' through 2029, ahead of Nov 5 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LITE is a ~$800+/share mid/large-cap AI optical-components name that no strategy lists. A volatile momentum name running into earnings would also likely trip gap, RSI or price filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic 'AI optical/photonics' basket (LITE, COHR, AAOI, CIEN) to the momentum universe, with a pre-earnings exclusion (skip entries within 3 trading days of the Nov 4-5 reports).
